text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Super League is poised to move the entire 1997 Rugby League World Cup to Australia forcing the ARL to suffer its international isolation from close range. The plan to switch the event from Great Britain has executive support from the World Board. Page 18.

Trainer Gai Waterhouse was nearly left without two runners in tomorrow's Caulfield races when Assertive Lass and Western Approaches were omitted from the field because of a clerical error. Waterhouse's representative lodged the acceptance form in accordance with the rules, but the paperwork was lost in the system. Page 16.

Australia's 10-year reign as surfing champions came to a disappointing end when the United States came from an almost impossible position to beat the lazy Aussies. Adding insult to injury, Brazil tipped Australia at the post, relegating them to third. Page 17.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia is set to join a new A$50 million superclub tournament pitting Australia's national league soccer teams against champion sides from Japan, the U.S. and other Pacific nations. The competition will begin as early as February. Page 44.

The renowned Tim Horan and Jason Little centre combination for the Wallabies is unlikely to be re-established until the Test against Scotland, with the Australian line-up for the opening rugby union Test against Italy remaining similar to the side that plyed South Africa. Page 44.

Parramatta forward Adam Ritson, who has been hospitalised for months after head injuries incurred from constant concussions, could be released from St Vincent's Private Hospital as early as this week, after encouraging signs of recovery. Page 44.
THE AGE

The Victoria Racing Club last night announced a review of drug testing after stewards allowed the Lee Freedman-trained champion three-year-old Encosta de Largo to race when it had returned an illegal blood reading. Page A1.

Australia's cricketers would have to snap out of an unaccountable and unprofessional lackadaisical attitude in their training, which led to a shock Test defeat by India on the weekend, if they were to maintain their world number 1 ranking this summer, according to coach Geoff Marsh. Page C8.

Australian and Aston Villa goal keeper Mark Bosnich should be banned by the English Football Association in the wake of his Nazi salute to Tottenham fans on Saturday, according to a British Member of Parliament. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

Canberra's Simon Dwight was the hero last night, burning Melbourne's Mark Bradtke and inspiring the Cannons to a first game win over the Tigers in the Basketball play-offs, 98/87. Dwight finished with 19 points, after overcoming a half-time Canberra deficit. Page 70.

Richmond Tigers want to join the AFL's Melbourne-based clubs who are drawn to play each other twice a year at the MCG. The Tigers want the "big three" of Collingwood, Carlton and Essendon to be expanded by one in recognition of their ability to draw big crowds. Page 70.

Cox Plate aspirant Saintly has been given special permission to gallop at Moonee Valley and will run solo over 1,600 metres, in an attempt to give the chestnut a few gallops at the track before the Plate next week, according to trainer Bart Cummings. Page 9.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian golfing superstar Greg Norman has revealed he will contest three Australian opens from next year without seeking a cent of appearance money or incentives, in an effort to dissipate any earlier criticisms surrounding his appearance in previous tournaments. Page 60.

Australian swimmers must be paid a wage if they are to remain competitive on the international circuit, according to Australian Swimming Inc president, and 1956 Olympian, Terry Gathercole. Gathercole said this would ensure our athletes can concentrate upon the 2000 Olympics and not finances. Page 58.

The South Queensland Crushers rugby league team is hopeful of a rescue package from the ARL to save the club from receivership. The club must pay A$840,000 by tomorrow to the Commonwealth Bank alone. Other debts have not yet been released. Page 56.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
